module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Representations as $p + 2^x + 11 \cdot 2^y$ with $p \equiv 1 \pmod 6$

Number of ways to write the $n$-th positive odd integer in the form $p + 2^x + 11 \cdot 2^y$
with $p$ a prime congruent to $1 \bmod 6$ and $x, y$ positive integers.
$$a(n) = \left|\left\{(p, x, y) : p + 2^x + 11 \cdot 2^y = 2n - 1 \text{ with } p \text{ prime},
p \equiv 1 \pmod 6, x, y \in \mathbb{Z}^+\right\}\right|.$$

*References:*
- [A157237](https://oeis.org/A157237)
- Z.-W. Sun, "Mixed sums of primes and other terms", arXiv preprint
  [arXiv:0901.3075](https://arxiv.org/abs/0901.3075) [math.NT], 2009.-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA157237

/-- Number of representations of $2n - 1$ as $p + 2^x + 11 \cdot 2^y$ with $p \equiv 1 \pmod 6$. -/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  if n = 0 then 0
  else
    let N := 2 * n - 1
    ∑ x ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N,
    ∑ y ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N,
      if 2 ^ x + 11 * 2 ^ y < N ∧
         (N - (2 ^ x + 11 * 2 ^ y)).Prime ∧
         (N - (2 ^ x + 11 * 2 ^ y)) % 6 = 1 then 1 else 0

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 1. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 0 := by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 2. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 0 := by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 16. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_16 : a 16 = 1 := by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 17. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_17 : a 17 = 1 := by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 18. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_18 : a 18 = 0 := by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 19. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_19 : a 19 = 2 := by decide

/--
On Feb. 24, 2009, Zhi-Wei Sun conjectured that $a(n) = 0$ if and only if $n < 16$ or
$n \in \{18, 21, 24, 51, 84, 1011, 59586\}$; in other words, except for
$35, 41, 47, 101, 167, 2021, 119171$, any odd integer greater than $30$ can be written as the
sum of a prime congruent to $1 \bmod 6$, a positive power of $2$ and eleven times a positive
power of $2$.-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    a n = 0 ↔ n ≤ 15 ∨ n = 18 ∨ n = 21 ∨ n = 24 ∨ n = 51 ∨ n = 84 ∨ n = 1011 ∨ n = 59586 := by
  sorry

end OeisA157237

reformulations.difference: OEIS defines a(n) as the number of triples <p,x,y> with p + 2^x + 11*2^y = 2n-1, p prime, p ≡ 1 (mod 6), x,y positive integers, and x,y are unbounded. The Lean sums an indicator over pairs (x,y) in Finset.Icc 1 N × Finset.Icc 1 N with N = 2n-1, requires 2^x + 11*2^y < N, and tests N - (2^x + 11*2^y) for primality and residue 1 mod 6. It also sets the junk value a 0 = 0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: p is determined by (x,y) as p = N - 2^x - 11*2^y, so counting triples is counting pairs. Any admissible pair has 2^x < N and 11*2^y < N, hence x < 2^x < N and y < N, so the bounded ranges drop no representation. p ≥ 7 > 0 forces 2^x + 11*2^y < N, so the strict guard excludes nothing and makes the truncated subtraction exact. The theorem only uses n > 0, so a 0 is never reached. I proved in Lean `a_eq : 0 < n → a n = {t : ℕ×ℕ×ℕ | t.1.Prime ∧ t.1 % 6 = 1 ∧ 0 < t.2.1 ∧ 0 < t.2.2 ∧ t.1 + 2^t.2.1 + 11*2^t.2.2 = 2*n - 1}.ncard`, using only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. From it I also proved `conjecture_iff_source`: the file's `conjecture` quantified over all n is equivalent to the literal OEIS statement 'for n ≥ 1, the triple set is empty iff n < 16 or n ∈ {18,21,24,51,84,1011,59586}'. As a numerical check, #eval of the Lean `a` matches the OEIS data for n = 1..60, and its zero set for n ≤ 200 is {1..15,18,21,24,51,84}.

review.notes:
I found no misformalization. The file states Sun's conjecture exactly as the OEIS comment gives it.

Checks performed:
(1) Lean proofs in scratch files, using only the standard axioms. `a_eq` shows `a n` equals the OEIS count of triples for n > 0. `conjecture_iff_source` shows `OeisA157237.conjecture` is equivalent to the literal source claim.
(2) The finite (←) direction is true. A C search confirms a(n) = 0 at every listed n, so the statement is not trivially false. It is not trivially provable either: the (→) direction is the open additive problem. The search results match #eval of the Lean definition on overlapping ranges.
(3) The test values a(1), a(2), a(16), a(17), a(18), a(19) match the OEIS data. The theorem docstring's odd numbers 35, 41, 47, 101, 167, 2021, 119171 are exactly 2n−1 for the listed n.

Status evidence consistently says 'open':
- The OEIS (rev. #9, Nov 2025) records the conjecture as verified below 1.5·10^8.
- All four full-benchmark runs of the 2026 OEIS Open benchmark (arXiv:2608.11941) failed on this problem.
- The released AlphaProof Nexus OEIS outputs do not include it.
- Extra evidence from this review: a segmented-sieve search, validated against the known zeros, finds no odd N < 10^11 outside the listed exceptions.

The arXiv reference 0901.3075 does not itself state the k = 11, p ≡ 1 (mod 6) conjecture; it discusses p + 2^a + k·2^b in general. The OEIS also links it, and the module docstring cites it only as a reference, so this is not a defect.

Out of scope: the sibling file FormalConjectures/OEIS/157225.lean may need a look. Its docstring says the analogous conjecture was disproved (a(716993899) = 0, arXiv:2608.11941), yet it keeps the positive statement under `research solved` with a formal_proof link. CONTRIBUTING says a problem solved in the negative should be stated as ¬P.
